statement: Every subspace of a normal topological space is normal, i.e. normality is a hereditary property.
definitions: Normal means T1 (every singleton closed) together with: any two disjoint closed sets have disjoint open neighbourhoods (i.e. T4). A subspace carries the subspace (relative) topology.
ground_truth_witness: The Tychonoff plank P = [0, omega_1] x [0, omega], the product of the two compact ordinal spaces of ordinals up to and including the first uncountable ordinal omega_1 and up to and including omega, is compact Hausdorff and hence normal. Deleting the single corner point (omega_1, omega) yields the deleted Tychonoff plank, which is not normal: the sets A = {omega_1} x [0, omega) (the right edge without the corner) and B = [0, omega_1) x {omega} (the top edge without the corner) are disjoint closed subsets of the deleted plank that cannot be enclosed in disjoint open sets, because any open set around B must, for each row, stretch past some countable ordinal, and the uncountable cofinality of omega_1 lets an open set around A dodge only boundedly many rows.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
verification_note: The argument rests on the uncountable cofinality of omega_1 (every countable subset is bounded), which admits no faithful finite computation; the script performs structural checks of the record only. Both the book and the secondary source state the non-normality of the deleted plank.
book_citation: Lynn Arthur Steen and J. Arthur Seebach Jr., Counterexamples in Topology, 2nd ed., Springer-Verlag, 1978 (Dover reprint, 1995), Examples 86 and 87 (Tychonoff plank; Deleted Tychonoff plank)

skeptic.objection: 'Normal' is not pinned and the difficulty depends on it. Under the weak convention (disjoint closed sets separable, no T1) the refutation is trivial: for any non-normal space X, adjoining a point p whose only neighbourhood is the whole space gives a normal space (every nonempty closed set contains p) with X as a subspace; verified on a 3-point X. Under the T4 convention (T1 + separation) the standard refutation needs the Tychonoff plank (or beta X of a non-normal Tychonoff space), a genuine argument. The claim is false under both conventions and the reference witness (deleted Tychonoff plank inside the compact Hausdorff plank; Steen-Seebach Ex. 86/87, standard) is valid under both. Admit with the T4 pin. No roster/surplus overlap (surplus topology items are Sierpinski T0/T1 and continuous bijection).
